artifacts.summary: 6-phase, 6.5-hour plan for the merge_targets.mcp deploy-engine mechanism, its durable regression harness, core documentation, and the settled obsidian-memory resolution.

memory_candidates.content: When a config file must hold both machine-generated and hand-written content, an additive deep-merge with per-producer tracked-unmerge is the correct idiom; a fully computed artifact regenerated wholesale is not. In this repo's extension deploy engine both idioms coexist in merge.lua: merge_settings/unmerge_settings only ever adds keys not already present and returns a tracked structure recording exactly what it added, persisted to the project-root state file so a later unload retracts only that producer's additions even across separate sessions. That single property delivers four requirements for free -- additive registration, per-producer retraction on unload, idempotent redeploy, and survival of hand-written user entries -- with no special casing. generate_opencode_json's computed-artifact idiom, by contrast, rebuilds the file from scratch on every change and therefore cannot preserve hand-written content at all, which is why it is gated behind a managed-marker file. Choose by asking whether any non-generated content can legitimately live in the target: if yes, additive-plus-tracked; if no, computed artifact.
